canonical_statement: Let M be a real continuous local martingale with M_0 = 0 on a filtered probability space and let T be a finite horizon. If E[exp((1/2) <M>_T)] is finite, then the stochastic exponential exp(M_t - (1/2) <M>_t), 0 <= t <= T, is a martingale (in particular its expectation is one).

canonical_formal_target.planned_shape: A finite-horizon theorem parameterized by a filtered probability space and a real continuous local martingale, using quadratic variation and stochastic exponential definitions

domain_and_universes: Provisional: a measurable sample type, real-valued time-indexed process, finite time horizon, filtration and probability measure; exact universes and time order are not frozen
quantifiers: filtered probability space and probability measure
real continuous local martingale M on [0,T]
hypotheses: the filtration and process satisfy the conditions needed to define continuous local martingales and quadratic variation
the expectation of exp((1/2) times the quadratic variation of M at T) is finite
conclusion: The Doléans stochastic exponential of M is a martingale through T; consequently its expectation at each t <= T is one

alternate_encodings.target: Brownian-integrand form: M_t = integral_0^t theta_s dW_s and E[exp((1/2) integral_0^T theta_s^2 ds)] < infinity
alternate_encodings.relationship: expected corollary after identifying quadratic variation

alternate_encodings.target: uniform integrability of the stopped stochastic-exponential family
alternate_encodings.relationship: proof-level strengthening commonly used to obtain the martingale conclusion

excluded_or_boundary_cases: No infinite horizon is claimed. T = 0 and the zero martingale remain required boundary probes. Jump-process variants and Kazamaki's distinct condition are outside the canonical root.
